siam-paragon.about: The flagship of Siam Piwat and The Mall Group at BTS Siam, and one of Thailand's largest malls. It pairs luxury fashion flagships and car showrooms with a big food floor, a gourmet supermarket and family attractions, which makes it a default stop for tourists and affluent Thais alike.
known_for: Gourmet Market and the Paragon Food Hall; the renovated food court brings together more than 100 well-known street-food names
SEA LIFE Bangkok Ocean World in the basement, which reports more than 2.5 million visitors a year
Luxury flagships, a 16-screen cineplex, Madame Tussauds and Royal Paragon Hall
suits: International and premium brands that want a Bangkok flagship with tourist exposure
Celebrated Thai street-food names that fit the food-hall format
Gift and specialty food brands that can sit near Gourmet Market
think_twice: First-time or thin-margin concepts: space is landlord-curated and fit-out standards and rents sit at the top of the market
Concepts that need a quiet, destination feel; peak-hour crowds are heavy

siam-center.about: Siam Piwat's fashion-led mall, opened in 1973 and long the launch pad for Thai designers. A full rebuild in 2013 turned it into a curated, collaborative space where the landlord works with each brand on custom storefronts and exclusive product.
known_for: The country's densest line-up of Thai designer brands
Custom storefronts and an exclusivity approach agreed with tenants
Art and design programming, including Bangkok Design Week venues
suits: Design-led cafés, dessert and drinks concepts aimed at young adults
Brands willing to co-create an exclusive store or menu with the landlord
think_twice: Large-format family restaurants: units are smaller and the crowd skews young
Operators who want a standard chain fit-out; the landlord expects a bespoke design

siam-discovery.about: A 40,000 sq m Siam Piwat mall rebuilt in 2016 by Japanese studio Nendo as 'The Exploratorium'. Instead of brand-by-brand stores, much of the floor is curated by theme, mixing Thai and Asian designers with global lifestyle names.
known_for: Nendo's interior and exterior redesign, a THB 4 billion overhaul
Curated 'lab' floors where a large share of space is run by Siam Piwat itself
Concept stores such as Loft and Issey Miyake, linked by bridges to Siam Center and MBK
suits: Concept F&B with a retail or design angle (coffee plus merchandise, collaborations)
Pop-ups and launches that benefit from a design-conscious audience
think_twice: Destination restaurants that rely on heavy evening footfall: before the rebuild the mall was known mostly as a walkway between MBK and Siam Center, so check traffic on your floor

mbk-center.about: Opened in 1985 as Mahboonkrong, MBK is an eight-storey, market-style mall with around 2,000 shops on land leased from Chulalongkorn University. It is Bangkok's best-known value mall, famous for its phone floor, souvenirs and a cheap food court, with Don Don Donki added in 2021.
known_for: Bargain fashion, souvenirs and the mobile-phone floor
A large, low-priced food court popular with tourists
A renovation plan that raised the share of space given to food and beverage
suits: Value and quick-service concepts, Thai street food and desserts
Tourist-facing snacks and takeaway with high volume and low ticket size
think_twice: Premium or fine-dining brands: the mall's identity is value-first
Concepts that need a polished, modern environment

siam-square-one.about: A seven-storey mall in Siam Square run by Chulalongkorn University's property office (PMCU), built on the site of the old Siam cinema. The upper floors are mostly restaurants and cafés, and in 2026 PMCU began repositioning it around global experience stores to revive Siam as the city's meeting point.
known_for: A dense cluster of buffet, shabu, Korean, Japanese and Thai restaurants on the upper floors
Affordable fashion on the lower floors for students and young shoppers
New experience stores such as ASICS and the first Thai branch of niko and ...
suits: Youth-focused casual dining: buffets, Korean and Japanese, cafés and desserts
Brands targeting students and first-jobbers from the Chula and Siam area
think_twice: Luxury or fine dining: the crowd and price points are mass-to-mid
Me-too concepts: competition between similar restaurants on the same floors is intense

centralworld.about: Central Pattana's flagship at Ratchaprasong, opened in 1989 as the World Trade Center and expanded in 2006 into one of the world's largest shopping complexes. Its forecourt hosts Bangkok's New Year countdown, and the complex includes offices, a hotel and a convention centre.
known_for: Sheer scale and a central location between BTS Siam and Chit Lom
A revamped 6,500 sq m Central Food Hall with a take-home zone of 40+ eateries
Groove, repositioned as an all-day outdoor courtyard of restaurants and bars
suits: Chains and international brands that need volume and visibility
Casual dining and dessert brands targeting office workers, Thai shoppers and tourists
Take-home and grab-and-go formats that fit the food-hall zone
think_twice: Niche concepts that rely on a curated, quiet setting; the mall is big and busy
Operators who cannot keep pace with the competition from hundreds of outlets in the same complex

central-chidlom.about: Central Department Store's flagship, opened in 1974 and relaunched in December 2024 as 'The Store of Bangkok' after a THB 4 billion renovation. Central Retail positions it as Thailand's leading luxury department store, aimed at the group's top spenders, families, Gen Y/Z, expats and tourists.
known_for: About 500 luxury brands across 60,000 sq m, around 10% of them exclusive
Food outlets tripled to more than 60 after the renovation, alongside the remodelled Central Food Hall
Average spend per visit reported at about twice the chain average
suits: Premium cafés, patisseries and gifting brands that want a luxury, high-spend audience
Chef-led or hotel-linked counters that fit a department-store food floor
think_twice: Value or mass concepts: the store is built around high-spend customers
Operators who need their own frontage and long hours; this is a department store with the landlord's rules on look and timing

gaysorn-village.about: Gaysorn Property's freehold cluster at the Ratchaprasong intersection: Gaysorn Centre (Thailand's first luxury mall), Gaysorn Tower and Gaysorn Amarin, the former Amarin Plaza rebuilt from 2022 and relaunched with mostly luxury and watch brands. The landlord pitches it as a 'placemaking' lifestyle village linked by skywalks.
known_for: Luxury fashion and watch boutiques, including concept stores
Gaysorn Amarin, reopened after a roughly THB 1 billion makeover
Office towers on site and a skywalk network to BTS Chit Lom
suits: Upscale cafés, wellness food and premium F&B for office workers and luxury shoppers
Brands that want a Ratchaprasong address without the scale of the big malls
think_twice: Mass-market concepts: footfall is smaller and skews high-income
Concepts that depend on evening crowds; much of the traffic is daytime office and shopping

platinum-fashion-mall.about: A wholesale and retail fashion mall in Pratunam, opened in 2000, often described as an indoor Chatuchak. Over a thousand small shops sell clothes and accessories to bargain hunters, tourists and resellers, with a large food centre on the top shopping floor.
known_for: Wholesale fashion, with discounts for buying several pieces
The sixth-floor food centre: cheap Thai, Indian, Chinese and halal dishes
Pratunam's dense tourist and trader traffic
suits: Fast, low-ticket Thai food, drinks and snacks for shoppers and traders
Halal and South Asian concepts serving Pratunam's international buyers
think_twice: Sit-down or premium dining: visitors come to shop fast and spend little on food
Concepts that need evening trade; the mall keeps early-closing wholesale hours

central-embassy.about: Central Group's ultra-luxury mall on the former British Embassy gardens on Ploenchit Road, with the Park Hyatt Bangkok in the tower above. Beyond luxury flagships it is known for Eathai, a basement Thai food hall, and Open House, a 7,000 sq m top-floor space mixing restaurants, a bookshop and co-working.
known_for: Luxury flagships under an AL_A-designed facade
Eathai, a Thai street-food hall with English menus
Open House: dining, books, art and co-working on the top floor
suits: Chef-driven and hotel-quality restaurants, premium cafés and bars
Thai street-food brands that can meet Eathai's standards for a tourist audience
think_twice: Mass-market concepts: the mall is designed for affluent locals and Park Hyatt guests
Brands that need high daily volume; luxury malls have lower footfall than CentralWorld or Siam

dusit-central-park.about: The Dusit Thani and Central Pattana mixed-use scheme at the Silom–Rama IV corner, on the site of the old Dusit Thani hotel. Its Central Park mall opened on 4 September 2025 and drew more than 70,000 visitors on day one, next to a new Dusit Thani hotel, residences and the Central Park Offices tower.
known_for: A roughly 7-rai roof park facing Lumpini Park
Parkside Food Hall with first-in-Thailand cafés and the flagship Tops Food Hall
Direct links to BTS Sala Daeng and MRT Si Lom
suits: International brands making their Thai debut; the landlord curates for 'firsts'
Premium casual dining and cafés for Silom office workers and affluent residents
Michelin-listed and well-known street-food names
think_twice: Me-too or value concepts: the tenant mix is curated for novelty and quality
Operators who need a proven trading history; the mall is new and still settling

central-pinklao.about: Central Pattana's Thonburi-side mall at the foot of Pinklao Bridge, rebuilt with an investment of more than THB 1.7 billion. CPN says traffic rose to about 80,000 visitors a day and sales by around 30% after the renovation, serving a high-spending residential catchment of more than 3 million people.
known_for: A Greek-column-inspired facade and naturally lit atrium
The 'Urban Living Room' food floor with Michelin-recognised and street-food names
An upgraded Tops Food Hall
suits: Family casual dining and Thai favourites for an established, affluent residential catchment
Street-food and Michelin-listed brands expanding beyond the CBD
think_twice: Tourist-led concepts: the trade is mostly local residents
Late-night formats; it is a neighbourhood mall, not a nightlife district

samyan-mitrtown.about: A mixed-use complex at the Sam Yan intersection on Rama IV, on Chulalongkorn University land, opened in 2019 and now run by Frasers Property Thailand. It was the first CBD mall with a 24-hour zone, built around food and learning for students, office workers and the surrounding Samyan community.
known_for: A 24-hour zone with cafés, diners and the free Samyan Co-op study space
A student and office-worker crowd from Chula and the Rama IV corridor
Easy MRT access next to the Banthat Thong street-food strip
suits: All-day and late-night casual dining, cafés and dessert spots
Value-to-mid price concepts aimed at students and young workers
think_twice: Premium sit-down dining: the core crowd is price-sensitive
Concepts that compete head-on with the Banthat Thong street-food strip next door

one-bangkok.about: Frasers Property's mixed-use district on Rama IV facing Lumpini Park, opened on 25 October 2024. Its retail runs across three linked zones, Parade, The Storeys and the luxury POST 1928 still to come, with offices, The Ritz-Carlton and Andaz hotels on site. The landlord reported more than 40 million visits and 96% retail occupancy by September 2026.
known_for: The 'Food Loop': around 250 dining options from fine dining to street food, including Thai debuts
Mitsukoshi Depachika food hall in Parade
A large office population on site to support weekday trade
suits: International restaurant brands entering Thailand that want a flagship next to a big office base
Premium casual dining, bars and all-day cafés for office workers and hotel guests
think_twice: Concepts that would be one of many similar restaurants; analysts have noted the dining mix overlaps with other big malls
Brands needing weekend family volume; much of the trade is weekday office-led

park-ventures-ecoplex.about: A LEED Platinum office and hotel tower at the Ploenchit–Wireless corner, completed in 2011 for TCC-linked Univentures, with the Okura Prestige Bangkok on its upper floors. A quarter of the site is landscaped green space, and the small retail podium links to BTS Phloen Chit.
known_for: Grade A offices with a sustainability label
The Okura Prestige hotel and its restaurants
A direct skywalk to BTS Phloen Chit
suits: Grab-and-go coffee, bakery and healthy lunch formats for office tenants
Premium breakfast and lunch concepts targeting Ploenchit offices
think_twice: Evening and weekend concepts: trade drops when offices close
Large-format restaurants; podium space is limited

the-unicorn.about: BTS Group's 51-storey mixed-use tower on Phaya Thai Road, opened in May 2023 with a direct link to BTS Phaya Thai and the Airport Rail Link. It combines Grade A offices, a retail podium with a food hub, an auditorium and the Eastin Grand Hotel Phayathai.
known_for: Direct connection to both BTS and the Airport Rail Link
A podium food hub serving office workers and hotel guests
LEED Gold-rated offices
suits: Quick-service lunch, coffee and grab-and-go formats for office and commuter traffic
Airport-traveller and hotel-guest snacks and casual dining
think_twice: Destination dining: the podium is a convenience stop, not a leisure destination
Concepts relying on weekend crowds

silom-complex.about: A Central Group office-and-retail complex at 191 Silom Road, opened in the early 1990s, with a Central Department Store, a Tops supermarket and a five-storey retail plaza. It is linked by skywalk to BTS Sala Daeng and is a short walk from MRT Si Lom, and travel guides describe it as the only mall on Silom Road.
known_for: Central Department Store and Tops supermarket for Silom office workers
Casual chains such as After You, Bonchon and Wine Connection
Direct BTS access in the heart of the original CBD
suits: Lunch and after-work casual dining for Silom office workers
Dessert, coffee and takeaway brands that live on commuter flow
think_twice: Concepts hoping for destination traffic: the mall is compact and described as quiet outside peak hours
Premium flagships, which now have a stronger option at Central Park across the road

robinson-bangrak.about: A Robinson department store on Charoen Krung Road, a short walk from BTS Saphan Taksin, in a 'sailboat' building by architect Sumet Jumsai that also holds a hotel. Robinson is Central Retail's mid-market chain; this branch serves riverside residents, hotel guests and office staff with a Tops supermarket and a food court.
known_for: Mid-market fashion, beauty and household goods
A Tops supermarket and a small food court
Location between the riverside hotels and the Sathorn–Silom CBD
suits: Value-to-mid chains and quick-service brands for residents and hotel guests
Grocery-adjacent takeaway and bakery formats
think_twice: Premium or destination dining: the store is mid-market and modest in footfall
Concepts that need a modern mall environment; the building is older

mahanakhon-cube.about: The six-storey retail block at the foot of King Power Mahanakhon, the 314 m tower by Ole Scheeren at BTS Chong Nonsi. King Power, which bought the retail, hotel and observatory parts in 2018, has turned the Cube into a food stop: Thai Taste Hub upstairs and Mahanakhon Eatery on the ground floor.
known_for: Thai Taste Hub: a curated set of legendary street-food and Michelin-recommended Thai restaurants
Mahanakhon Eatery, a shared dining hall of about eight restaurants
Footfall from the Mahanakhon SkyWalk observation deck
suits: Well-known Thai street-food brands looking for a CBD branch with tourist traffic
Quick casual dining for Sathorn–Silom office workers
think_twice: Large-format restaurants: the Cube's floor plates are small
Brands that cannot join King Power's curated hall format

empire-tower.about: Asset World Corporation's 'The Empire' at the Sathorn–Narathiwat corner: three linked office towers of up to 58 storeys, completed in 1998 and described by AWC as Thailand's largest office complex. A skybridge connects it to BTS Chong Nonsi and BRT Sathorn, and the podium holds a supermarket, restaurants, cafés and a large food pavilion.
known_for: Tens of thousands of office workers in one complex
A food pavilion, supermarket and convenience retail for tenants
Skybridge links to BTS Chong Nonsi and BRT Sathorn
suits: Breakfast, lunch and coffee formats that live on office headcount
Food-pavilion stalls and grab-and-go concepts with fast turnover
think_twice: Evening and weekend concepts: trade is tied to office hours
Destination or leisure dining; the podium serves tenants first

sathorn-square.about: Frasers Property's 40-storey Grade A office tower at the Sathorn–Narathiwat corner, completed in 2011 with a direct link to BTS Chong Nonsi. Frasers revamped the building in 2024, adding health-food and international restaurants and hangout space to the podium.
known_for: Direct BTS Chong Nonsi link at the CBD's main office junction
A 2024 asset-enhancement revamp of the podium
Neighbours include King Power Mahanakhon and W Bangkok
suits: Healthy lunch, coffee and premium grab-and-go for office tenants
After-work bars and casual dining tied to the Sathorn office crowd
think_twice: Weekend-led concepts: the trade is weekday office traffic
Large or family-format restaurants; the podium is small

terminal-21-asok.about: An airport-themed mall at the Asok interchange, opened in 2011, where each floor is styled after a world city. It sits under Grande Centre Point Sukhumvit, connects to BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit, and holds around 600 shops, a cinema and Gourmet Market.
known_for: Pier 21, one of central Bangkok's cheapest and busiest food courts
City-themed floors that make it a tourist photo stop
Direct links to BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit
suits: Affordable Thai and Asian food stalls with very high turnover
Casual, family-friendly chains and dessert brands for tourists and office workers
think_twice: Premium dining: the mall's food draw is value
Concepts competing on price with Pier 21; food-court prices set expectations in the building

exchange-tower.about: A 42-storey office tower at the Asok–Sukhumvit intersection, completed in 2006, with a five-storey retail podium linked by a covered skybridge to BTS Asok. The podium mixes banks and services with cafés and international restaurants for the tower's corporate tenants.
known_for: Direct skybridge to BTS Asok, a short walk from MRT Sukhumvit
Multinational office tenants and serviced offices
A small podium of cafés, restaurants and services
suits: Coffee, breakfast and quick lunch formats for office workers
Business-lunch restaurants near the Asok interchange
think_twice: Weekend or leisure concepts: Terminal 21 next door captures that traffic
Large-footprint restaurants; the podium is modest

the-emquartier.about: The Mall Group's second EM District mall, opened in May 2015 opposite Emporium at BTS Phrom Phong. It is split into the Glass, Helix and Waterfall Quartiers; the spiralling Helix holds around 50 restaurants, and the mall adds Gourmet Market, a food hall, an IMAX cinema and an indoor garden.
known_for: The Helix dining spiral with roughly 50 restaurants
Gourmet Market and Quartier Food Hall
Luxury fashion and a 40 m indoor waterfall
suits: Premium casual and chef-led restaurants targeting Sukhumvit's affluent Thais, expats and tourists
Japanese, Korean and international chains seeking a flagship in the EM District
think_twice: Value concepts: price points and fit-out standards are high
Brands that would sit on the upper Helix floors without a draw; footfall thins as you climb

the-emporium.about: The first EM District mall, opened by The Mall Group in 1997 beside Benjasiri Park at BTS Phrom Phong. It is the district's most department-store-like building, with luxury brands, an upscale food hall and Gourmet Market serving Sukhumvit's established affluent and expatriate residents.
known_for: Luxury brands and The Emporium department store
Emporium Food Hall and Gourmet Market
A long-standing customer base of affluent locals and expats
suits: Premium cafés, bakeries and refined casual dining for mature, high-income shoppers
Gourmet and specialty food brands that fit the Gourmet Market audience
think_twice: Youth-led or trend concepts: the crowd is older than at EmQuartier or EmSphere
Mass-market brands

emsphere.about: The third EM District mall, opened by The Mall Group on 1 December 2023 between Sukhumvit Soi 22 and 24, opposite EmQuartier. Its glass-dome design houses retail, entertainment and dining zones such as Em Market, and the landlord has pushed late-night trade to make the district a 'city that never sleeps'.
known_for: A large, new building of roughly 200,000 sq m
Em Market food zone and dining-led floors
Late-night entertainment programming across the EM District
suits: Trend-led and late-night F&B, bars and dessert concepts for young adults
International brands making a Bangkok debut close to EmQuartier
think_twice: Concepts that need a long trading history before committing; the mall is still building its pattern
Value brands; the EM District is positioned premium

gateway-ekamai.about: A Japanese-themed mall opened in 2012 at BTS Ekkamai, now owned by TCC's Asset World Corporation. Its eight floors hold around 400 shops, with a Japanese Town dining zone that introduced several original Japanese brands to Thailand, plus a supermarket, an IT zone and family-oriented learning centres.
known_for: Japanese restaurants and cafés on floor M
Direct skybridge to BTS Ekkamai
Family services: tutoring, an indoor playground and a supermarket
suits: Japanese restaurant brands entering Thailand, especially mid-priced chains
Family casual dining for the Ekkamai and Sukhumvit residential catchment
think_twice: Concepts that need strong upper-floor traffic: reviewers describe the upper floors as quiet
Fashion-led or premium concepts; the mall's draw is food and daily needs

j-avenue-thonglor.about: One of Bangkok's earliest community malls, at the mouth of Thonglor Soi 15, serving the area's affluent Thai and Japanese residents. It is small and food-led, with long-running names such as Greyhound Cafe and After You alongside a supermarket, banks and services.
known_for: A loyal neighbourhood crowd in one of Bangkok's wealthiest districts
Popular cafés, dessert shops and Japanese restaurants
Late-opening supermarket and everyday services
suits: Dessert, café and casual Japanese concepts aimed at affluent residents
Brands testing a Thonglor address before a mall roll-out
think_twice: Concepts that need rail traffic: it is a long walk from BTS Thong Lo
Large-format restaurants; units are small

the-commons-thonglor.about: A four-level, open-air community mall on Thonglor Soi 17, opened by the siblings behind Roast and Roots Coffee. The founders wanted 'a community first, then a mall', so the ground-floor Market works like a curated food hall of artisan and home-grown vendors, with Roast on the top floor.
known_for: The Market: independent food and drink vendors around shared seating
Roast and Roots Coffee as anchors
No big chains; a curated, neighbourhood feel
suits: Independent and chef-led concepts that fit a curated market format
Specialty coffee, bakery and dessert brands for Thonglor's affluent crowd
think_twice: Chains: the landlord avoids them by design
Brands that need mall-style air-conditioned comfort; much of the space is open-air

seenspace-thonglor.about: An early Thonglor community mall on Soi 13, built around an open courtyard of restaurants, bars and cafés that made it a pre-club hangout for the neighbourhood's young, affluent crowd. Parts of the complex have since been re-launched with new concepts, such as Pirate Saloon on the first floor.
known_for: A courtyard where diners order from several bars and restaurants
An evening and nightlife crowd of Thais and expats rather than tourists
Re-launches of space as the mall ages
suits: Bars, casual dining and late-night concepts aimed at Thonglor's young professionals
Operators who can create their own pull rather than relying on mall traffic
think_twice: Daytime or family concepts: the trade skews to evenings
Brands that need a busy, well-maintained mall around them; newer Thonglor malls compete hard

donki-mall-thonglor.about: A Japanese-themed mall on Ekkamai Soi 5 that opened in February 2019 as the home of Thailand's first Don Don Donki, the Japanese discount store, with over 30 Japanese-origin tenants. Donki has since closed some other Bangkok branches, but the Thong Lor flagship is reported as still trading.
known_for: Don Don Donki's Thai flagship, with a late-night Japanese food zone
Japanese restaurants, cafés, drugstores and an indoor sports centre
A Japanese and Thai residential catchment in Thonglor–Ekkamai
suits: Japanese food brands and grab-and-go concepts that benefit from Donki's traffic
Late-night snack and drink formats
think_twice: Non-Japanese concepts that would feel out of place in the tenant mix
Operators who need rail access; the mall sits off the main road between BTS stations

rain-hill.about: A six-level, open-air community mall on Sukhumvit at Soi 47, between BTS Phrom Phong and Thong Lo, styled around a tropical vertical garden. Its tenants lean towards Japanese and Western dining, wine bars and cafés for the surrounding residents and office workers.
known_for: A vertical-garden, open-air design on the main road
Japanese restaurants, Wine Connection and cafés
Evening trade from the Thonglor–Phrom Phong residential belt
suits: Japanese and Western casual dining, wine and dessert concepts for affluent locals and expats
Neighbourhood cafés and after-work dining
think_twice: Concepts that need climate-controlled comfort or heavy daytime traffic; Inside Retail noted community malls like this struggled to recover after the pandemic

the-parq.about: A THB 20 billion office-and-retail scheme by TCC Assets and Frasers Property at the Rama IV–Ratchadaphisek corner, next to the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center and Benjakitti Park. Its retail podium, The PARQ Life, opened in September 2020 with about 12,000 sq m and more than 60 shops, about 60% of them restaurants and cafés.
known_for: LEED and WELL-certified Grade A offices, with healthy-eating options
Restaurants and cafés making up most of the podium
Proximity to QSNCC and Benjakitti Forest Park
suits: Healthy lunch, salad and coffee concepts for office tenants
Event-driven trade from conventions at QSNCC next door
think_twice: Weekend-dependent concepts: trade follows the office and convention calendar
Tourist-led formats; visitors are mostly workers and event-goers

fyi-center.about: A TCC Group office building on Rama IV by MRT Queen Sirikit, one of the first pieces of the group's office and convention node around QSNCC, alongside ThaiBev Quarter and The PARQ. Its ground-level retail serves the building's office workers and convention visitors.
known_for: Office population on the Rama IV corridor
Short walk to MRT and the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center
suits: Coffee, breakfast and lunch formats for office workers
Grab-and-go for convention visitors
think_twice: Evening and weekend concepts
Anything needing a large dining room; retail space is limited

w-district.about: A mixed community site at Sukhumvit Soi 71 by BTS Phra Khanong, completed in late 2014, anchored by condominium towers and known above all for W Market, an open-air evening food court with dozens of stalls and bars. Its owners have not ruled out redeveloping the market site for condos.
known_for: W Market's international street food and live music at weekends
An expat and middle-class Thai crowd
A short walk from BTS Phra Khanong
suits: Street-food and bar concepts testing demand at low cost
International food stalls aimed at expats
think_twice: Any long fit-out investment: the market's long-term future is uncertain
Daytime concepts; the market comes alive after 6 pm

habito-mall.about: Sansiri's first community mall, at the centre of its T77 neighbourhood on Sukhumvit 77 (On Nut), opened in 2016 with about 10,000 sq m of retail. It serves around 5,000 households in Sansiri's surrounding condos plus the Bangkok Prep international school campus, with a shuttle to BTS On Nut.
known_for: A planned residential community with a Japanese-influenced mix of tenants
Restaurants, cafés, a food court and food trucks
A co-working and co-creation space and seasonal markets
suits: Neighbourhood casual dining, Japanese and café concepts for young residents and families
Brands testing a captive residential catchment at moderate rent
think_twice: Concepts that need walk-in rail traffic; access relies on a shuttle from BTS On Nut
Destination or premium dining; the trade is local

true-digital-park.about: CP Group's tech and start-up campus beside BTS Punnawithi on Sukhumvit 101, billed as Southeast Asia's largest start-up hub. The East phase opened in 2019 and the West in 2022; the lifestyle and retail floors were later revamped by CP Future City to serve office tenants and the surrounding Bangkok CyberTech District.
known_for: A large daytime workforce of tech companies and start-ups
Retail and dining on floors 1–3 with pop-up events
Direct access from BTS Punnawithi
suits: Coffee, healthy lunch and casual dining for tech workers
Food-tech and new-concept pilots that fit the start-up audience
think_twice: Weekend and family concepts: traffic follows the working week
Premium destination dining; the area is still emerging

central-bangna.about: Central Pattana's veteran mall on Bang Na–Trat Road, now in its biggest transformation in three decades. CPN is turning the 50-rai site into a mixed-use district of about 300,000 sq m with offices and housing, with 'The New Central Bangna' due by the end of 2026; CPN says more than 85% of its customers are affluent families.
known_for: An affluent family customer base, per CPN's loyalty data
A Tops Food Hall ranked among the chain's top five by sales
A Food Patio of Michelin-listed and long-established Thai eateries
suits: Family casual dining, Thai favourites and dessert brands for Bangna's affluent households
Brands that want to open with the relaunch and its fresh tenant mix
think_twice: Operators who cannot cope with construction disruption during the transformation
Tourist-led concepts; the catchment is residential

imperial-world-samrong.about: An older multi-level shopping complex on Sukhumvit in Samrong, Samut Prakan, run by the Imperial Group and reached by skywalk from BTS Samrong. It serves the local working and residential population with budget shops, food courts and a cinema, next to the busy Samrong market.
known_for: Budget retail and two food courts
Skywalk access from BTS Samrong
A dense local market area around the mall
suits: Value Thai food, quick-service and snack kiosks
Brands targeting Samut Prakan's working households
think_twice: Premium or trend-led concepts: the customer base is value-driven
Concepts relying on a modern mall environment; the building is dated

mega-bangna.about: A low-rise super-regional mall on Bang Na–Trat Road at km 8, opened in 2012 around Thailand's first IKEA. It is now an equal joint venture between Central Pattana and IKEA's Ikano group, which reported a record 60 million visits in 2025, full occupancy, and a THB 6 billion expansion due by Q3 2028.
known_for: Anchors: IKEA, Central Department Store, HomePro, Big C and Mega Cineplex
About 165,000 visitors a day, per the owners
A planned 2,000 sq m 'Mega Loft' social dining zone in the expansion
suits: Family chains and casual dining that need car-borne weekend volume
Brands expanding east toward Suvarnabhumi with a big-box anchor next door
